subject: Proposed remedy-scaling & degradation tolerance for enterprise SLA
messages:
From: Simon Leung <simon.leung@bigfin.tech>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@bigfin.tech; procurement@bigfin.tech
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA — monthly remedy cap and short degradation handling

Neha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the performance looked good. Before legal signs off on the contract, procurement raised two items we need clarity on:

1) Remedy cap: Our legal team is pushing for a lower monthly service credit exposure than the flat 100% cap in your template. They want a hard monetary cap per month tied to average spend, not an open-ended percentage.

2) Degradation vs outage: We operate a latency-sensitive trading assistant; a sustained 99th-percentile latency spike for 20 minutes could be more harmful to us than a short outage. We need a clearer definition of "degradation" (impacting SLA) vs "outage" (full unavailability) and how credits scale for degradation windows.

Can Redwood propose a structured alternative that limits maximum payout while giving us confidence on operational behavior and remediation timelines? Also please confirm if scheduled cluster rebalances (30–90s brief tail-latency bumps) will be treated as maintenance carveouts or normal operations.

-Simon
CRO, BigFin Technologies

Attachment: none
From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Leung <simon.leung@bigfin.tech>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, contracts@bigfin.tech
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — monthly remedy cap and short degradation handling

Simon — thanks for the clear note and the context on the trading assistant. I pulled together a proposal (attached) that tries to balance your procurement team's need for a monetary cap and your ops team's need for predictable behavior during degradation. High level:

- Tiered remedy scale (monthly): rather than a single-percent cap we propose a sliding remedy schedule capped at a fixed USD amount tied to committed spend. For example:
  • Tier A (>=99.95% monthly uptime): 0–5% monthly credit (pro-rata).
  • Tier B (99.90%–99.95%): 5%–25% credit scaling linearly with lost availability.
  • Tier C (<99.90%): additional escalated credits up to the monetary cap (example: up to $250k/month, tied to committed monthly minimum).

- Degradation definition: we propose to treat a degradation event as any 99th-percentile latency spike above 3x baseline sustained for >=15 consecutive minutes and impacting >10% of requests. Full outage remains defined as complete inability to serve control-plane or data-plane requests to the production model endpoint. Credits will be applied proportionally for degradation windows (not binary).

- Short rebalances (30–90s tail bumps): we recommend classifying brief, scheduled rebalances as maintenance carveouts if pre-scheduled in the rolling maintenance calendar OR if they are run-time, automated node rebalances under the Dedicated plan up to 2x/month per customer and are <120s each. Unscheduled rebalances that cause sustained >5m consumer impact would be treated as degradations/outages per the definition above.

I attached a draft "Remedy Scaling" PDF and an operations runbook excerpt that shows how we detect, notify, and remediate degradations. A few asks from our side:
- Can procurement agree to tie the monetary cap to a committed monthly spend band? (we have a template table in the PDF)
- Would your ops team accept our diagnostic window (15m) to trigger scaled credits, or do you need a lower threshold?

If this looks reasonable I can route a redline for your legal team and prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Thanks — want to make this work for you.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Subject: Fwd: Redwood SLA — internal: review remedy-scaling draft for BigFin

Neha — quick internal note before we send the redline:

Forwarding Simon's ask and your proposed structure. A few internal comments:
- Ben: confirm that the detection pipeline can reliably surface 99th percentile over 15m windows and generate automated PagerDuty alerts plus an ops ticket with pre-populated diagnostics. If not, we should relax the time threshold or make the first-tier credits paused until manual confirmation.
- Laura: commercial question — the proposed monetary cap example ($250k/mo at X commit) is reasonable, but legal will want a ceiling formula in the contract (e.g., greater of 3x monthly fee or fixed $X). Let's avoid open-ended language.

Ben — do you have any evidence from staged runs that rebalances are typically sub-60s tail bumps? If so we can tighten the carveout to <90s and keep scheduled rebalances off the remedy table.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — quick ops confirmation:

- We can reliably compute 99th-percentile latency over rolling 15-minute windows and emit an automated degradation alert. We've validated this in the Dedicated cluster runbook — attaching a short extract to the runbook spreadsheet included in Neha's email.
- Rebalance behavior: on Dedicated pools we routinely see <45s tail-latency bumps for automated rebalances under normal load; during peak burst patterns this can stretch up to ~110s. For BigFin, whose traffic is bursty, I recommend we leave the unscheduled rebalance threshold at 5 minutes (if exceeded, treat as degradation). For scheduled rebalances, we can keep them carveouts if pre-notified in the rolling calendar and if each event is <120s.

I'll co-sign the proposed detection thresholds, but suggest we add a clause for a "rapid mitigation" timeline: within 10 minutes of alert, Redwood will attempt automated remediation (cache priming, KV warming, burst autoscale), and will update BigFin every 15 minutes until service returns to baseline.

Ben Carter
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — monthly remedy cap and short degradation handling

Simon — thanks for the patience. Based on internal review we've updated the draft and are prepared to offer the following commercial/ops commitments for the Dedicated deployment: 

1) Monetary cap: final cap will be defined in the amendment as the greater of (a) 3x the customer's committed monthly fee OR (b) a fixed $250k/month cap for customers with commitments >= $500k/month. Table in the attached PDF maps other bands.

2) Degradation handling: we will use 99th-percentile >3x baseline over 15 consecutive minutes and affecting >10% of requests as the threshold for degradation credits. Credits scale proportionally by minute after the first 15-minute window.

3) Short rebalances: scheduled, pre-notified rebalances <120s are carveouts. Unscheduled rebalances that cause >5 minutes of impact are treated per the degradation rules.

4) Rapid mitigation & communication: upon automated degradation alert Redwood will kick off mitigation within 10 minutes and provide 15-minute status updates until baseline recovery.

Next steps: if procurement is comfortable with the cap formula above, I'll send a redline and a DocuSign amendment link. If you need a lower detection window than 15m, tell us which window you want and we'll review feasibility with Reliability.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
